questions.q: A 35-year-old farmer presents with a painless ulcer on the dorsum of his right hand with satellite lesions and regional lymphadenopathy. Gram stain of discharge shows gram-positive rods in 'medusa head' pattern. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Cutaneous anthrax presents as a painless eschar with surrounding edema. Bacillus anthracis forms the 'medusa head' pattern on culture. The painless nature and Gram-positive rod morphology are characteristic.

questions.q: A 28-year-old immunocompetent patient presents with grouped vesicles on an erythematous base along the T5 dermatome. The patient reports severe burning pain preceding the rash by 3 days. Which antiviral is the drug of choice and what is the ideal window for initiation?
opts: Acyclovir 800mg 5x/day within 72 hours of rash onset
questions.exp: Herpes zoster (shingles) is treated with oral Acyclovir 800mg 5 times daily for 7 days. Treatment should be initiated within 72 hours of rash onset to reduce viral replication and risk of post-herpetic neuralgia.

questions.q: A 40-year-old patient with leprosy on MDT presents with sudden onset of tender erythematous nodules over the limbs, fever, and joint pain. Nerve function assessment shows new impairment. This reaction is characterized by which immunological mechanism?
questions.exp: Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL) or Type 2 lepra reaction is mediated by immune complex (Type III hypersensitivity) with complement activation. It occurs in BL/LL leprosy. Type 1 reactions are Type IV (cell-mediated) in nature.

questions.q: A 22-year-old sexually active female presents with painless genital ulcer with indurated base and regional lymphadenopathy. Dark field microscopy of ulcer exudate shows motile corkscrew-shaped organisms. What is the treatment of choice?
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM single dose
questions.exp: Primary syphilis (Treponema pallidum) is treated with Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM as a single dose. Dark field microscopy showing spirochetes confirms Treponema pallidum. This remains the gold standard treatment.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman presents with butterfly-shaped malar rash, photosensitivity, and oral ulcers. ANA is positive with anti-dsDNA antibodies. She develops painful blistering lesions in sun-exposed areas. Which diagnosis explains this complication?
questions.exp: Bullous SLE is a vesiculobullous disorder occurring in SLE patients, characterized by autoantibodies to type VII collagen (same as EBA). Blisters occur in sun-exposed areas. IgG deposits at the BMZ are seen on DIF.

questions.q: A 65-year-old diabetic man presents with tense bullae on an erythematous base on the flexural areas and trunk. Nikolsky sign is negative. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 deposition at the dermoepidermal junction. What is the first-line treatment?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid (BP) presents with tense bullae, negative Nikolsky sign, and linear IgG/C3 at BMZ on DIF. Oral corticosteroids are first-line treatment. Dapsone can be used as steroid-sparing agent. Rituximab is for refractory cases.

questions.q: A 70-year-old man presents with a slow-growing pearlescent papule with rolled edges and central ulceration on the nose, present for 2 years. Dermoscopy shows arborizing vessels. Histology shows palisading nuclei at the periphery. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) is the most common skin malignancy. Classic features include pearlescent papule with rolled edges, central ulceration (rodent ulcer), arborizing vessels on dermoscopy, and peripheral palisading on histology.

questions.q: A patient on carbamazepine for 3 weeks develops widespread blistering involving >30% BSA with mucosal involvement, fever, and constitutional symptoms. There is full thickness epidermal necrosis on biopsy. What is the Severity of Illness Score for TEN (SCORTEN) used for?
questions.exp: SCORTEN (Severity of Illness Score for TEN) is a validated scoring system using 7 parameters (age >40, malignancy, HR >120, BSA>10%, BUN>28mg/dL, glucose>252mg/dL, bicarbonate<20mEq/L) to predict mortality in TEN/SJS. Each parameter scores 1 point.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman develops a fixed drug eruption on the lip every time she takes ibuprofen. She is now pregnant and needs analgesia. What is the safest alternative and what is the pathomechanism of her condition?
opts: Paracetamol; CD8+ T cells in the dermis releasing IFN-gamma upon drug re-exposure
Tramadol; mast cell degranulation with IgE involvement
Codeine; CD4+ T helper cells causing delayed reaction
Aspirin; Type II cytotoxic antibody-mediated reaction
questions.exp: Fixed drug eruption involves intraepidermal CD8+ T cells (non-circulating effector memory T cells) that become activated upon drug re-exposure, releasing IFN-gamma causing keratinocyte apoptosis. Paracetamol is safe in pregnancy for analgesia.

questions.q: A 25-year-old male student presents with circular patches of hair loss with exclamation mark hairs and a positive pull test. There is no scarring. What is the most likely diagnosis and what does a positive pull test indicate?
opts: Alopecia areata; active disease with telogen hairs easily pulled at the margin
Tinea capitis; active fungal infection progressing
questions.exp: Alopecia areata presents with non-scarring patches, exclamation mark hairs (broader distal end), and positive pull test (>6 hairs) at the margin indicating active disease. The pull test at the periphery of the patch shows easily extracted telogen hairs.

questions.q: A 45-year-old HIV-positive patient presents with painless, whitish, corrugated plaques on the lateral border of the tongue that cannot be scraped off. What is the causative agent?
questions.exp: Oral hairy leukoplakia is caused by EBV (Epstein-Barr virus) and presents as corrugated white plaques on the lateral tongue in immunocompromised patients. Unlike oral candidiasis, it cannot be scraped off. It is an AIDS-defining opportunistic infection.

questions.q: A 3-year-old child presents with honey-colored crusted lesions around the nose and mouth. KOH mount is negative. Tzanck smear shows no multinucleated giant cells. Which organism is most likely responsible?
questions.exp: Non-bullous impetigo presents with honey-colored crusted lesions around the nose and mouth, most commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus (or S. pyogenes). The negative KOH and Tzanck smear rule out fungal and viral etiology. S. aureus is now the most common cause.

questions.q: A 50-year-old woman on hydroxychloroquine for SLE develops skin darkening in a reticular pattern over her lower legs. She also has livedo reticularis and thrombocytopenia. Which condition should be suspected?
questions.exp: Antiphospholipid antibody syndrome (APS) presents with livedo reticularis, thrombosis, thrombocytopenia, and skin necrosis/ulcers. The reticular pattern of skin changes along with the systemic features is characteristic. APS can occur secondary to SLE.

questions.q: A 30-year-old patient presents with violaceous flat-topped polygonal papules with Wickham's striae on the flexor wrists and ankles. Oral examination shows lacy white pattern on buccal mucosa. What is the first-line treatment for symptomatic cutaneous lichen planus?
questions.exp: Lichen planus is characterized by 5 P's: pruritic, purple, polygonal, planar, papules. Wickham's striae are pathognomonic. High-potency topical corticosteroids (clobetasol) are first-line for cutaneous LP. Oral LP may require systemic treatment.

questions.q: A dermatology trainee is counseling a patient with psoriasis about biological therapy. The patient has extensive plaque psoriasis with PASI 18 and DLQI 12. Which biologic targets TNF-α and requires tuberculosis screening before initiation?
questions.exp: Adalimumab is an anti-TNF-α monoclonal antibody approved for moderate-to-severe psoriasis. TNF-α inhibitors require TB screening (IGRA or Mantoux test) before initiation as they increase risk of TB reactivation. Secukinumab and Ixekizumab target IL-17A; Guselkumab targets IL-23.

questions.q: A 20-year-old woman presents with hypopigmented macules on the cheeks, trunk, and limbs with decreased sensation. Slit-skin smear is negative. Biopsy shows granulomas around dermal nerves and appendages without AFB. What is the classification?
questions.exp: Tuberculoid leprosy (TT) presents with well-defined hypopigmented macules, loss of sensation, thickened peripheral nerves, negative smear, and well-formed granulomas with few/absent bacilli on histology. TT has strong CMI response (high Th1).

questions.q: A 35-year-old male presents with progressive symmetric peripheral neuropathy, thickening of ear lobes, and widespread hypopigmented infiltrated plaques with a leonine facies. Slit skin smear shows Bacteriological Index of 5+. What is the correct MDT regimen?
opts: Rifampicin 600mg monthly, Clofazimine 300mg monthly + 50mg daily, Dapsone 100mg daily for 12 months
Rifampicin 600mg monthly, Dapsone 100mg daily for 6 months
Dapsone 100mg daily, Clofazimine 50mg daily for 24 months
Rifampicin 600mg daily, Dapsone 100mg BD for 12 months
questions.exp: Lepromatous leprosy (MB leprosy) requires Multi-drug therapy: Rifampicin 600mg once monthly (supervised), Clofazimine 300mg once monthly (supervised) + 50mg daily (unsupervised), Dapsone 100mg daily for 12 months as per WHO MB-MDT.

questions.q: A 42-year-old woman has painful ulcers on her vulva and oral mucosa for 3 months. She also has hypopyon in the right eye and a positive pathergy test. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Behcet's disease is characterized by recurrent oral ulcers + genital ulcers + uveitis (the classic triad). Pathergy test (prick site develops a pustule within 24-48 hours) is positive in ~60% of patients. It is associated with HLA-B51.

questions.q: A patient presents with a firm, flesh-colored plaque on the shin with dimple sign (central dimpling on lateral compression). Histology shows bland spindle cells in storiform pattern with collagen trapped at the periphery. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Dermatofibroma (fibrous histiocytoma) presents with firm papule/plaque showing positive dimple sign (Fitzpatrick sign). Histology shows spindle cells in storiform pattern with trapped collagen at periphery. CD34 negative (unlike DFSP which is CD34 positive).

questions.q: A 55-year-old man with 30 pack-year smoking history presents with a rapidly growing nodule on the lower lip that developed over 6 weeks and shows central keratin-filled crater. What is the likely diagnosis and management?
opts: Keratoacanthoma; excision due to potential for malignant transformation to SCC
questions.exp: Keratoacanthoma presents as rapidly growing crateriform nodule with central keratinous plug, classically on sun-exposed sites. Although some regress spontaneously, excision is recommended due to histological similarity to SCC and potential for malignant transformation.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman with dermatomyositis develops heliotrope rash, Gottron's papules, and proximal muscle weakness. Which serology is associated with interstitial lung disease in dermatomyositis?
questions.exp: Anti-Jo-1 antibodies are associated with antisynthetase syndrome: myositis + ILD + mechanic's hands + Raynaud's + arthritis. Anti-Mi-2 is associated with classic DM with good prognosis. Anti-MDA5 with amyopathic DM and rapidly progressive ILD. Anti-TIF1-γ with cancer-associated myositis.

questions.q: A patient with type 2 diabetes presents with velvety hyperpigmented thickening in the axilla, neck, and groin. Skin tag-like papillomas are present. What investigation should be prioritized?
opts: Fasting blood glucose and insulin resistance markers
questions.exp: Acanthosis nigricans is strongly associated with insulin resistance. In a diabetic patient, assessing glycemic control and insulin resistance (fasting glucose, HbA1c, HOMA-IR) is the priority. Malignancy-associated AN should be suspected when onset is rapid, extensive, or associated with mucosal and palmar involvement.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman presents with a painful nodule on her right great toe that increases in size. X-ray shows soft tissue swelling. The lesion shows a rosette pattern of epithelioid histiocytes on biopsy with Splendore-Hoeppli phenomenon. What is the causative organism?
questions.exp: Sporotrichosis (Sporothrix schenckii) presents as a nodular lymphangitis pattern. The Splendore-Hoeppli phenomenon (asteroid bodies surrounded by eosinophilic material) may be seen. Treatment is itraconazole. It is a dimorphic fungus and a subcutaneous mycosis.

questions.q: A 60-year-old man presents with recurrent superficial erosions and crusted lesions on the scalp, face, and trunk. Nikolsky sign is positive. DIF shows intercellular IgG deposition in a fishnet pattern in the epidermis. What is the target antigen?
questions.exp: Pemphigus foliaceus targets Desmoglein 1 (expressed mainly in the superficial epidermis), causing subcorneal blistering with erosions and crusts. Nikolsky sign positive. DIF shows IgG in intercellular space. Pemphigus vulgaris targets Dsg3 (mucosal) and/or Dsg1 (cutaneous).

questions.q: During a Wood's lamp examination, a patient with pityriasis versicolor shows which color of fluorescence?
questions.exp: Pityriasis versicolor caused by Malassezia furfur shows golden-yellow or yellowish-green fluorescence under Wood's lamp. Erythrasma (Corynebacterium minutissimum) shows coral-red fluorescence. Tinea capitis (M. canis) shows blue-green fluorescence.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with widespread scaly plaques over extensor surfaces with nail pitting, oil drop sign, and onycholysis. She has been using a new beta-blocker for hypertension. What is the relationship between the drug and her condition?
opts: Beta-blockers can exacerbate psoriasis by inhibiting beta-adrenergic receptors reducing cAMP
Beta-blockers cause psoriasis de novo through immune activation
Beta-blockers are safe in psoriasis as they act only on cardiac receptors
The relationship is coincidental; psoriasis is purely genetic
questions.exp: Beta-blockers worsen psoriasis by blocking beta-adrenergic receptors, which reduces intracellular cAMP. Low cAMP promotes keratinocyte proliferation and inflammatory cytokine production. Other psoriasis-aggravating drugs: lithium, antimalarials, NSAIDs, alcohol.

questions.q: A 16-year-old presents with multiple tender erythematous nodules on the shins. She had a sore throat 2 weeks ago. Serology confirms streptococcal infection. What is the diagnosis and what does biopsy typically show?
opts: Erythema nodosum; septal panniculitis with neutrophilic infiltrate and Miescher radial granulomas
Erythema induratum; lobular panniculitis with caseous necrosis
Nodular vasculitis; lobular panniculitis with vasculitis
Subcutaneous fat necrosis; lobular panniculitis with calcium deposits
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum is the most common panniculitis, presenting as tender erythematous nodules on shins. It is a septal panniculitis (inflammation in fibrous septa). Biopsy shows septal thickening with neutrophils, lymphocytes, and Miescher radial granulomas (histiocytes around central star-like cleft).

questions.q: A patient undergoing patch testing shows a +++ reaction at the test site 96 hours after application. This positive patch test result indicates what type of hypersensitivity?
questions.exp: Patch testing detects Type IV hypersensitivity (allergic contact dermatitis). Reactions are read at 48 and 96 hours (D2 and D4). +++ reaction indicates vesiculation and bullae at the test site. The reaction is mediated by sensitized CD4+ Th1 and CD8+ T cells.

questions.q: A 50-year-old patient with chronic plaque psoriasis requires a biological agent but has a history of multiple sclerosis. Which biologic class is contraindicated?
questions.exp: TNF-alpha inhibitors are contraindicated in demyelinating disorders like multiple sclerosis, as TNF-α plays a role in oligodendrocyte and myelin protection. IL-17 and IL-23 inhibitors are safer alternatives for psoriasis in patients with demyelinating disease.

questions.q: A 35-year-old patient presents with a 2cm pigmented lesion on the back. Dermoscopy shows irregular pigment network, blue-white veil, regression structures, and atypical vessels. What is the most important next step?
opts: Excisional biopsy with 2mm margin for histopathological confirmation
Wide local excision with 1cm margin immediately
questions.exp: Dermoscopic features (blue-white veil, irregular pigment network, atypical vessels, regression) are suspicious for melanoma. The first step is excisional biopsy with narrow margins (1-2mm) to obtain the entire lesion for histopathological diagnosis and Breslow thickness measurement, which guides subsequent management.

questions.q: A 28-year-old construction worker presents with pruritic vesicular eruption on the dorsum of hands and forearms after working with wet cement. Patch test is positive to potassium dichromate. What is the diagnosis?
opts: Irritant contact dermatitis to cement alkali
questions.exp: Cement is the most common cause of occupational allergic contact dermatitis due to hexavalent chromium (chromate). Positive patch test to potassium dichromate (standard screening series) confirms the diagnosis. This must be differentiated from irritant contact dermatitis (ICD) to cement alkali which is non-immunological.
